name: validation-baseline-v4
note:
Sentence Build scored as a construction, and completeness added as a weighted dimension. Both change scored values, so this supersedes v3 rather than restating it.

Sentence Build was scored by the same word-accuracy path as Read Aloud, whose denominator is the reference length alone. Padding was therefore free: saying the sentence twice scored exactly as well as saying it once, on a task whose entire point is the arrangement. It now scores coverage (were the given words used, multiset) and order (longest common subsequence over the longer of the two word lists) at 0.2/0.8, reports the characteristic failure as one word_order error rather than as a pile of substitutions the candidate did not make, and reads rubric['also_correct'] so a second legitimate arrangement becomes a content change rather than a code change. Read Aloud and Repeat Sentence are untouched.

Completeness measures how much of the answer that was asked for arrived: reference coverage for scripted items, speech duration against the item's stated minimum for open ones, capped at 1.0 so talking longer cannot earn marks. It returns unscored, with a reason, where the item never said what complete would look like -- scoring the bank's silence as an incomplete answer would fail candidates for our own missing data. Every other dimension judges the quality of what was said; none noticed that a third of it was missing.

Weights: pronunciation .22->.20, accuracy .22->.20, fluency .18->.17, latency .12->.11, disfluency .09->.08, grammar .10->.09, content .07 unchanged, completeness .08 new. Sums to 1.0. The 0.08 and the 0.2/0.8 construction split are judgements, not findings -- no data stands behind either, and the study this baseline exists for is what should move them.

No validation study data has been collected against v3, so nothing is orphaned by this re-cut.
